bib.title: Reading Wikipedia to Answer Open-Domain Questions
bib.venue: ACL 2017 (55th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics), pages 1870-1879

question: Can open-domain factoid QA be done with Wikipedia as the only knowledge source by combining document retrieval with a neural machine-comprehension reader (machine reading at scale)?
hypothesis: A simple non-learned retriever plus a strong RNN reader, trained with multitask learning and distant supervision across several QA datasets, gives an effective single full system.
contributions: Define machine reading at scale (MRS): retrieve from over 5 million Wikipedia articles, then read to find the answer span
DrQA: a TF-IDF plus hashed-bigram Document Retriever and a multi-layer BiLSTM Document Reader
Document Reader reaches 70.0 EM / 79.0 F1 on the SQuAD test set
Distant supervision and multitask learning over SQuAD, CuratedTREC, WebQuestions and WikiMovies improve the full system

method.summary: DrQA retrieves the top 5 Wikipedia articles with a TF-IDF bag-of-words and hashed-bigram retriever (no machine learning), then runs a 3-layer BiLSTM reader on every paragraph to predict start and end of an answer span, taking the argmax of unnormalised span scores across paragraphs. The reader is trained on SQuAD and on distantly supervised paragraphs for three other QA datasets.
method.task: open-domain extractive QA over Wikipedia (machine reading at scale)

datasets.name: English Wikipedia 2016-12-21 dump
datasets.preprocessing: WikiExtractor; plain text only, lists and figures stripped; disambiguation, list, index and outline pages discarded

datasets.name: SQuAD
datasets.size: 87,599 train questions (87k), 10,570 dev (10k); hidden test set
datasets.split: train for the reader; dev for open-domain eval (questions only, no paragraph)

datasets.name: CuratedTREC
datasets.size: 2,180 questions; Table 2: 1,486 train (no paragraph), 3,464 DS train, 694 test
datasets.source: TREC 1999-2002, curated by Baudis and Sedivy 2015

datasets.name: WebQuestions
datasets.size: Table 2: 3,778 train (no paragraph), 4,602 DS train, 2,032 test

datasets.name: WikiMovies
datasets.size: 96k QA pairs; Table 2: 96,185 train (no paragraph), 36,301 DS train, 9,952 test

datasets.name: Distantly supervised (DS) training data
datasets.source: built from the QA pairs with the Document Retriever
datasets.preprocessing: top 5 articles per question; drop paragraphs without exact answer match, shorter than 25 or longer than 1500 characters, or lacking question named entities; score answer positions by unigram and bigram overlap in a 20 token window; keep up to top 5 paragraphs; discard if zero overlap

models.name: DrQA Document Retriever
models.architecture: inverted index with TF-IDF weighted bag-of-words, hashed bigram counts

other.hash: unsigned murmur3 into 2^24 bins (printed '224' in the extracted text)

models.name: DrQA Document Reader
models.architecture: multi-layer bidirectional LSTM with exact-match, token (POS, NER, TF) and aligned question embedding features; bilinear start and end classifiers
models.init_from: GloVe 300-d 840B Web crawl embeddings, mostly fixed; only the 1000 most frequent question words fine-tuned

other.full_wikipedia_variant: streamlined: no CoreNLP f_token features or lemmas for f_exact match

models.name: YodaQA
models.architecture: open-source pipeline using web, Freebase, DBpedia, Wikipedia

other.note: numbers copied from its benchmarks wiki

training.objective: two independent classifiers for span start and end (softmax over paragraph tokens); the loss is not written out
training.batch_size: 32 examples per minibatch, sorted by paragraph length
training.dropout: p = 0.3 on word embeddings and all LSTM hidden units

other.variants: SQuAD only; Fine-tune (DS): pretrain on SQuAD then fine-tune per dataset on its DS set; Multitask (DS): one model trained jointly on SQuAD and all DS sets

inference.decoding: best span i..i' maximising P_start(i) x P_end(i'), i' <= i+15; unnormalised exponential scores, argmax over all paragraph spans of the retrieved documents
inference.samples: single model, single run; no seeds reported
inference.retrieval: top 5 articles from the Document Retriever; WebQuestions and WikiMovies answers restricted to the candidate list (1.6 million Freebase entity strings for WebQuestions)

metrics.name: Retrieval answer-in-top-5
metrics.definition: % of questions for which an answer text span appears in at least one of the top 5 pages

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: weighted average of precision and recall at token level

metrics.name: Top-1 exact-match accuracy, full Wikipedia
metrics.definition: top-1 EM using SQuAD eval script

baselines: Okapi BM25 and bag-of-embeddings cosine retrieval (worse, numbers not given)
eval.protocol: SQuAD reader on dev and hidden test (test run by Rajpurkar); open-domain eval on SQuAD dev, CuratedTREC, WebQuestions and WikiMovies test sets; no significance tests

limits: Training of reader paragraphs is independent; no aggregation over paragraphs or documents in training (authors' future work i)
Retriever and reader are not trained end to end (future work ii)
SQuAD questions were written with a paragraph in mind and are ambiguous without context, so the drop to 27.1 partly reflects the dataset
Retrieval metric checks string presence of the answer, not relevance
No learning rate, epochs, seeds, hardware or compute reported; no code URL in the text
BM25 and bag-of-embeddings retrieval said to be worse, with no numbers
Full-Wikipedia numbers are far below machine comprehension numbers and below YodaQA on two datasets

terms.definition: combining the challenges of document retrieval with machine comprehension: retrieve the few relevant articles among more than 5 million, then scan them to identify the answer
automatically associating Wikipedia paragraphs with question-answer pairs that have no paragraph, following Mintz et al. 2009
